मासेषु शून्यसंज्ञकाः [?— शून्यनक्षत्रचक्रम्: मुद्रित तालिका (चैत्रादि १२ मासों × शून्यतिथि/शून्यनक्षत्र) OCR में विच्छिन्न एवं अपाठ्य]

विषमतिथिषु दग्धलग्नानि

पक्षादितस्त्वोजतिथौ घटैणौ[?] मृगेन्द्रनक्रौ मिथुनाङ्गने च ।
झष[?]कर्कहरी हयान्त्यौ गोऽन्त्यौ च नेष्टे तिथिशून्यलये ॥ १७ ॥

(पक्षादि) प्रतिपदासे लेकर विषम तिथियोंमें ये लग्न शून्य होते हैं। जैसे—प्रतिपदामें मकर[?], तृ० में मकर, सिंह; पं० मिथुन, कन्या; स० धनु, कर्क; न० सिंह, कर्क; ए० धनु, मीन। ये शून्यलग्न शुभकार्योंमें वर्ज्य हैं ॥ १७ ॥ (इन्द्रवज्रा)

दुष्टयोगानां शुभकृत्यावश्यकत्वे परिहारः

नारदः—तिथयो माशून्याश्च शून्यलग्नानि यान्यपि ।
मध्यदेशे विवर्ज्यानि न दुष्यन्तीतरेषु तु ॥ १८ ॥
पङ्ग्वन्धकाणलग्नानि मासशून्याश्च राशयः ।
गौडमाल्वयोस्त्याज्या अन्यदेशे न गर्हिताः ॥ १९ ॥

जो मासशून्य तिथ्यादि कहे हैं इनके निमित्त विशेषता नारद कहते हैं कि, मासशून्य तिथि तथा जो शून्य लग्न कहे हैं वे भी मध्यदेशहीमें वर्ज्य हैं, अन्य देशोंमें इनका दोष नहीं; तथा पंगु, अन्ध, काण लग्न (जो विवाह-प्रकरणमें कहे हैं) और मासशून्य राशि गौडदेश (मारव)[?], मल्बार (केरल)[?] देशमें वर्जित करने, अन्य देशोंमें निन्द्य नहीं है ॥ १८ ॥ १९ ॥ (अनुष्टुप्)।

शुभकार्येषु सिद्धिदानामपि हस्तार्कादियोगानां निन्द्यत्वम्

वर्जयेत् सर्वकार्येषु हस्तार्कं पञ्चमीतिथौ ।

(8) Muhūrta-Cintāmaṇi [Śubhāśubha-prakaraṇa]

THE VOID-DESIGNATED [STARS] IN THE MONTHS
[The printed table of month-wise śūnya nakṣatras is broken up and illegible in the scan — not rendered.]

THE BURNT (DAGDHA) LAGNAS ON ODD TITHIS

(17) Counting from the beginning of the fortnight, on the odd tithis (lunar days) these lagnas (ascendants) [are void]: Ghaṭa (Kumbha) and Eṇa[?]; Mṛgendra (Siṃha) and Nakra (Makara); Mithuna and Aṅganā (Kanyā); Jhaṣa[?] (Mīna), Karka and Hari (Siṃha); Haya (Dhanus) and Antya (Mīna); Go (Vṛṣa) and Antya (Mīna). The lagna void for a given tithi is inauspicious.

[ṭīkā] Reckoning from the pratipadā (first day of the fortnight), on the odd tithis these lagnas are void: on the first, Makara[?]; on the third, Makara and Siṃha; on the fifth, Mithuna and Kanyā; on the seventh, Dhanus and Karka; on the ninth, Siṃha and Karka; on the eleventh, Dhanus and Mīna. These void lagnas are to be shunned in auspicious works. (17) (Indravajrā)

PARIHĀRA (CANCELLATION) OF THE MALEFIC YOGAS WHEN AN AUSPICIOUS ACT IS UNAVOIDABLE

(18) Nārada [says]: those tithis that are month-void, and likewise those lagnas that are declared void — they are to be shunned in Madhyadeśa [alone]; among other [peoples/regions] they do not vitiate.
(19) The lame (paṅgu), blind (andha) and one-eyed (kāṇa) lagnas, and the month-void rāśis (signs), are to be avoided in Gauḍa and Mālava; in another country they are not censured.

[ṭīkā] Regarding the month-void tithis and the rest that have been stated, Nārada states a qualification: the month-void tithi and the void lagnas that have been described are to be shunned in Madhyadeśa only — in other countries they carry no doṣa (affliction). Likewise the paṅgu, andha and kāṇa lagnas (which are described in the marriage chapter) and the month-void rāśi are to be rejected in the Gauḍa country ([Mārava?][?]) and [a second region — the OCR here reads as either Mālava or, alternatively, Malabar (Kerala); the mūla verse (19, translated above) is unambiguous for Gauḍa and Mālava, so that pairing is retained as the primary reading, but the ṭīkā's own restatement at this exact point is genuinely uncertain and may have specified a different or additional region][?]; in other countries they are not blameworthy. (18–19) (Anuṣṭubh)

THE CENSURABILITY OF THE HASTĀRKA AND SIMILAR YOGAS EVEN THOUGH THEY BESTOW SUCCESS IN AUSPICIOUS WORKS

(20ab) In all undertakings one should reject the Hasta–Arka [combination — Hasta nakṣatra on a Sunday] when it falls on the fifth tithi.

(1)-(4) as originally noted: the month-wise śūnya-nakṣatra table is illegible and not rendered; verse 17's pratipadā sign-pair and the 'झष' supply are uncertain; the ṭīkā's tithi-by-tithi list is itself corrupt. (5) NEW: the ṭīkā's restatement of verse 19's Gauḍa/Mālava rule contains a second region name that the original OCR renders ambiguously — possibly 'Mārava' as a gloss on Gauḍa, and possibly 'Malabar (Kerala)' rather than 'Mālava' for the second region. The verse itself (19) is unambiguous and correctly gives Gauḍa+Mālava; only the ṭīkā's own restatement of that same rule is uncertain at this specific point, and is now marked [?] rather than silently resolved.

और (गंगा) भागीरथीके देशोंमें लुप्तसंवत्सरका दोष है, अन्यत्र नहीं। आचार्यान्तरमतसे बृहस्पति-शुक्रके सम-सप्तम (एकसे दूसरी सातवीं राशि) में होनेपर भी उक्त देशोंमें अस्तके तुल्य दोष है ॥ ५३ ॥ (वंशस्थ)।

वारप्रवृत्तिः

पादोनरेखापरपूर्वयोजनैः[?] ...ऋणधनोनास्तिथयो[?] दिनार्धतः ।
ऊनाधिकास्तद्विवरोद्भवैः[?] पटेर्ध्वं तथाधो दिनपप्रवेशनम् ॥ ५४ ॥

लंकासे सुमेरपर्यन्त एक समसूत्र बांधकर उसके नीचे जो जो आवें वह मध्य रेखा है। जहांसे उस रेखागत कोई देश समीप हो, वह जितने योजन (चार कोशका एक) हो, वे देशांतर योजन कहते हैं। उन योजनोंके चतुर्थांश घटाकर पंद्रह (१५) में (न्यूनाधिक)—पर योजन हो तो जोड़ना, पूर्व हो तो घटाना। जिस दिन वारप्रवेश देखना है उस दिनके दिनार्धमें (न्यूनाधिक) पन्द्रहमें न्यून वा अधिक किया गया जो देशांतर है, वह (१५) से अधिक हो तो उसमें १५ घटाना; यदि १५ से न्यून हो तो [दिनार्ध] से उसे घटा देना—यह वारप्रवृत्ति होती है। उसमें भी स्मरण रखना चाहिये कि दिनार्ध संस्कारविशिष्ट अंकसे यदि १५ न्यून हो तो सूर्योदयसे पीछे; उक्त पलोंमें यदि १५ से न्यून वह गणितागत अंक हो तो सूर्योदयसे प्रथम ही वार प्रवेश जानना।
उदाहरण—काशीपुरी प्राक् मध्यरेखा कुरुक्षेत्रसे ६३ योजन है; चौथाई घटाया ४७।१५; प्राक्योजन होनेसे १५ में पल ४७ घटाये तो १४।१३ हुए; दिनार्ध १७।२ से न्यून होनेसे १४।१३ घटाया, २।४९ शेष रहा। दिनार्धसे न्यून गणितागत अंक होनेसे सूर्योदयसे पीछे २।४९ में वारप्रवेश होगा ॥ ५४ ॥ (उपजाति)।

वारप्रवृत्तिप्रयोजनपुरस्सरा होराः

वारादेर्घटिकाद्विघ्नाः[?] स्वाक्ष...[?]शेषवर्जिताः ।
सैकास्त...[?] नगैः कालहोरेशा दिनपात्क्रमात् ॥ ५५ ॥

[संख्याको] द्विगुण कर २ जगह स्थापन करना; एक जगह (५) से भा[ग]

(22) Muhūrta-Cintāmaṇi [Śubhāśubha-prakaraṇa]

[ṭīkā, completing verse 53] …and in the countries of the Bhāgīrathī (Gaṅgā) the doṣa (affliction) of the lost year obtains, and nowhere else. By the opinion of other ācāryas, when Jupiter and Venus stand in mutual seventh signs (from one to the seventh from it) there is, in the said countries, a doṣa equal to that of combustion. (53) (Vaṃśastha)

THE COMMENCEMENT OF THE WEEKDAY

(54) [Take] the yojanas east or west of the meridian, less a quarter[?]; …subtracted or added[?] from half the day; less or more by the difference thence arising[?] — [thus is found] the entry of the day-lord, above or below [sunrise].

[ṭīkā] Stretch a straight line from Laṅkā to Sumeru; whatever places fall beneath it constitute the central meridian. The distance in yojanas (one yojana being four kośa) by which any country lies from that meridian is called the deśāntara-yojanas. Deduct a quarter of those yojanas, and [apply the remainder] to fifteen (15) — adding if the place is WEST [of the meridian], subtracting if EAST. On the day for which the weekday-entry is to be found, in the half-day of that day, [take] the deśāntara thus made less or greater than fifteen: if it exceeds 15, subtract 15 from it; if it is less than 15, subtract it from [the half-day] — this gives the commencement of the weekday. One should further bear in mind: if the deśāntara-corrected half-day figure comes out less than 15, the weekday-entry falls after sunrise; whereas if the computed figure itself (in the palas just described) is less than 15, the weekday-entry is to be reckoned as falling before sunrise. [?] Example: the city of Kāśī lies 63 yojanas east of the central meridian at Kurukṣetra; deducting a quarter gives 47;15. Being an eastern longitude, 47 palas are subtracted from 15, giving 14;13. Since this is less than the half-day 17;2, subtracting 14;13 leaves a remainder of 2;49. As the computed figure is less than the half-day, the weekday-entry will occur 2;49 after sunrise. (54) (Upajāti)

THE HORĀS, PREFACED BY THE PURPOSE OF THE WEEKDAY-COMMENCEMENT

(55) [The count] from the weekday, in ghaṭikās, doubled[?]; …[?] with the remainder removed; increased by one …[?]; [divided] by seven (naga) — [thus] the lords of the kāla-horās, from the day-lord, in order.

[ṭīkā] Double [the number] and place it in two positions; in one position divi[de] by (5) [continues in the next chunk]
ocr_review_note: CORRECTED 2026-08-03 after independent verification (verifier findings: (1) east/west sign of the deśāntara correction was inverted — the Hindi unambiguously reads 'पर योजन हो तो जोड़ना, पूर्व हो तो घटाना' = add if WEST, subtract if EAST, which the worked Kāśī example itself already confirmed (Kāśī is east of the meridian and 47 is subtracted) even though the general rule as first translated said the opposite; now corrected to match both the ṭīkā's own wording and its own worked example. (2) A full rule-bearing sentence on whether weekday-entry falls before or after sunrise was present in cleaned_devanagari_text but dropped from content_en; it has been restored, rendered as literally as the compressed Hindi allows, and marked [?] since the underlying procedural clause is terse enough that independent re-derivation was not possible this pass.) Four or more other flagged points remain as originally noted: verses 54 and 55's mūla are badly corrupt and the renderings are governed by the ṭīkā's worked procedure, not the verse text.

[ṭīkā] (concluding verse 109) Praveśa (entry) — the entry of a new bride is of four kinds: sapūrva, apūrva, dvandva, and bhaya [?]; it is to be done in the mṛdu (soft) and dhruva (fixed) nakṣatras. If the entry is made in the kṣipra (swift) or cara (movable) nakṣatras, there will be a further departure; in Viśākhā there is destruction of the wife; in Kṛttikā, destruction of the house by fire and the like; in the dāruṇa (harsh) nakṣatras, loss of a son; in the ugra (fierce) nakṣatras, one's own destruction. || 109 || (metre: Upajāti of the Jagatī class)

(verses 110–112: the collected doṣas. The mūla is a compressed catalogue of technical names and is substantially corrupt; the translation follows the ṭīkā, which decodes each term. Flagged readings are marked.)

(verse 110) The śūlas arising from the ayana (solstitial half-year), the nakṣatra, the month, the tithi, the kāla and the vāra; the cara [?]; [the doṣa of] Venus and Mercury facing [the traveller] and the [adverse] quarters they hold [?]; [the doṣas] named after Venus, retrogression and the rest, and the parigha-daṇḍa; likewise the menses of one's wife, ritual impurity, and festivals and the like [that bar departure].

(verse 111) Mṛta-pakṣa; the riktā tithis and those numbering twelve and six; the weekdays of Saturn, the Sun and Mars; also the Moon standing behind or to the left, and likewise [Mahāḍala] [?]; the pañcaka beginning with Dhaniṣṭhā; and also the Abhijit muhūrta, for a southward [journey].

(verse 112) As lagna: the natal lagna, the natal sign [?], the eighth [sign], and the sixth place [from the lagna] and its lord [?]; also Aquarius and Pisces as lagna or as navāṃśa, and a pṛṣṭhodaya (hind-rising) sign; [a lagna] falling in the nakṣatra of the quarter behind [?]; Saturn in the tenth, and Venus (kāvya) in the seventh; retrograde planets in a kendra, and the weekday of a retrograde planet [?] — and the doṣas declared for marriage: [all these] are not desired.

Here ends the eleventh chapter, on Travel, in the illustrious Muhūrta-Cintāmaṇi. || 11 ||

[ṭīkā] The collection of doṣas (doṣa-samuccaya): ayana-śūla, per 'saumyāyane sūryam' etc.; māsa-śūla, of two kinds — for the signs in groups of three beginning with Taurus, the śūla towards the east and the rest, that is one; for the months in groups of three beginning with Kārttika, the śūla towards the east and the rest — these two are [called] kapāla and kaṇṭaka; nakṣatra-śūla and vāra-śūla, per 'na pūrvadiśī' etc.; tithi-śūla, per 'navabhūmyeti'; Venus and Mercury facing [the traveller], per 'sitajñadikkapā' etc.; vakra, asta and parājita and the rest, per 'śukravakrāstanīceti'; parigha-daṇḍa, per 'pūrvādiṣu catur' etc.; the sight of one's own wife's menses; ritual impurity (aśauca); the bar of a marriage or the like; mṛta-pakṣa, per 'tamobhuktatārā' etc.; the riktā tithis 4, 9, 14, and up to 12 [and] 6 [?], and the 15th and 30th tithis; the weekdays of Saturn, the Sun and Mars; and the Moon gone behind; Mahāḍala (the doṣa reckoned by remainder 7 counting from the Sun's nakṣatra to the Moon's, defined at Muhūrta-Cintāmaṇi 3.25 above), per 'raverbhe' etc.; the pañcaka beginning with Dhaniṣṭhā; the Abhijit muhūrta for a southward [journey]; and the natal lagna, the natal rāśi, the eighth lagna, the lagna of an enemy's sign, the sixth place from the lagna and its lord, [and reckoned] from one's own natal rāśi — [the ṭīkā continues in the next chunk]
